proposals.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (about 5 eV) lithium-ion insulator. Its phosphate anion is hard to oxidize, so it should resist the 4.0 V operating potential better than halides or silicates.

proposals.motivation: Earlier Li3PO4 evaluation showed that a wide-gap, Li-rich, sulfide-compatible insulator is the right design target. LiF extends this to a different anion family while keeping the same criteria.
